An interesting take. Based on history, it’s true that technology tends not to eliminate jobs, but to reshape them or move them to something else. However, there’s never been a technology so capable and improving so quickly, so it’s quite difficult to predict how things will evolve. If there’s a company that has basically the same job a bunch of times, and a person with a tool can be 5 times as efficient, that seems likely to cause a job hit (like programmers, for example). Or if the technology can do things like drive a lot more cheaply, while still as safely, that seems like an elevator operator type job — what else is the guy in the car box going to do besides drive? Plus there’s the point that this is the first time there’s been a technology which can not only displace a job, but replace the new job created because of that.
